correctness.rationale: The standard 28-vertex cubic Coxeter graph was independently generated from harmonic disjoint duads of P1(F7). The 196009 independent subsets (including the empty face) were enumerated independently with the exact face-size histogram and alternating sum -7. Using the source-specified Fano model pivot order but independently implementing the face-poset matching, verified 98001 augmented pairs, seven critical six-faces and a full 196009-node acyclic Hasse DAG (1319752 cover relations). This certifies the integral nonequivariant wedge of seven S6 used as an input, not only an Euler count. Independently enumerated all 336 distinct projective matrices; for each graph action computed the fixed-face signed Lefschetz sum through quotient-orbit conflict graphs and checked it equals epsilon(det)*(fixed points on P1-1). All eight class rows and multiplicities were matched, including trace +1 on 8-cycles. Character determines the rational module epsilon tensor augmentation, irreducible by 2-transitivity and with zero PGL invariants. Integral equivariant structure is not asserted.

value.rationale: The Coxeter graph is a canonical highly symmetric cubic graph, and its homology rank seven admits inequivalent actions. The complete, irreducible, quadratically twisted natural PGL2(7) module and absence of invariant classes are concrete structural information not obtainable from a seven-sphere wedge or automorphism-group order.

limitations: The theorem identifies rational PGL2(F7) homology, not its integral equivariant lattice.
Full-group identification uses established Coxeter graph automorphism theorem, while all indicated 336 transformations were checked independently.
Finite exact enumeration is not an infinite-family theorem.
